1. Case 1: RA-associated necrobiotic nodules with pneumothorax
A young seropositive RA patient on immunosuppressants presented with acute dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain. CTPA excluded pulmonary embolism; absence of fever and biopsy-proven necrobiotic granulomas with pleural extension argue against infection and drug toxicity. Cavitary lung lesions and bilateral pneumothorax, together with biopsy findings and negative CTPA, strongly support rheumatoid arthritis-associated necrobiotic nodules as the leading diagnosis. Classic RA pleuritis/ILD, opportunistic infection, pneumonia, and drug-induced toxicity are less likely. BAL, HRCT pattern, and PFTs remain pending to exclude secondary infection or concurrent ILD and refine final diagnosis.
